title: NY State Assembly · District 59
area: Brooklyn: Canarsie, Flatlands, Georgetown, Mill Basin, Marine Park, Bergen Beach, and Gerritsen Beach

context.text: Incumbent Jaime Williams (D) defeated Jibreel Jalloh 66.0% to 33.8% in the June 23, 2026 Democratic primary. Jalloh remains on the November ballot on the Working Families Party line, so the general election is a rematch between the two.

candidates.name: Jaime Williams
candidates.currentRole: NY State Assembly Member, District 59 (since April 2016)

summary.text: Jaime Williams is the incumbent Democratic and Conservative Party candidate for Assembly District 59, first elected in an April 2016 special election to fill a vacancy. A social worker and substance-abuse counselor by training, she worked for Catholic Charities before entering the Assembly, where she chairs the Real Property Taxation Committee. She won the June 2026 Democratic primary over Jibreel Jalloh.

background.text: According to the Assembly's biography, Williams studied at Kingsborough Community College, then earned a bachelor's degree in social work from York College and a master's degree in social work from Fordham University. She later returned to Kingsborough to earn a CASAC-T certificate as an Alcohol and Substance Abuse Counselor with a specialization in gambling counseling.
She has more than eight years of experience counseling women and children who were victims of domestic violence, and clients who were HIV-positive with a history of substance abuse.

She served as Community Project Director for Brooklyn East at Catholic Charities, providing outreach programs in Brownsville, East New York, Canarsie, and Mill Basin, and worked with Catholic Charities on relief for residents of Canarsie, Bergen Beach, Gerritsen Beach, and Coney Island after Superstorm Sandy.

She is a past member of the 69th Precinct Community Council, the Mill Basin Civic Association, and Brooklyn Community Board 18, and is a member of the Canarsie Lions Club and NYC's Community Emergency Response Team (CERT).

Williams took office after a special election on April 19, 2016, to fill the seat left vacant when Roxanne Persaud was elected to the state Senate; she defeated Republican Jeffrey J. Ferretti. She won a full term in November 2016 with 78.1% of the vote against Ferretti.
Her 2025-2026 committee assignments are Agriculture, Environmental Conservation, Governmental Operations, Real Property Taxation (chair), and Transportation.
The Assembly biography says she has led humanitarian relief missions to aid several countries and territories in the Caribbean, and spearheaded a mission to Kentucky after the December 2021 tornado.
In the June 23, 2026 Democratic primary she defeated Jibreel Jalloh, 66.0% to 33.8%, and she advanced from the Conservative Party primary, which was canceled.

record.text: Chairs the Assembly's Real Property Taxation Committee (2023-2024 and 2025-2026 sessions); also serves on the Agriculture, Environmental Conservation, Governmental Operations, and Transportation committees.

Prime sponsor of A03887, which would give a 50% discount on Manhattan central business district tolls, fees, and other congestion-pricing charges to residents of designated transit deserts; referred to the Corporations, Authorities and Commissions Committee, no floor vote as of September 2026.

Prime sponsor of A03856, which would require the Triborough Bridge and Tunnel Authority to reimburse transit-desert residents 100% of central business district tolls when traveling for medical treatment or religious services; referred to committee, no floor vote as of September 2026.

candidates.name: Jibreel Jalloh
candidates.ballotNote: Lost the June 23, 2026 Democratic primary to incumbent Jaime Williams; remains on the November general-election ballot on the Working Families Party line.

summary.text: Jibreel Jalloh is a Brooklyn-born community organizer and nonprofit leader running for Assembly District 59 on the Working Families Party line after losing the June 2026 Democratic primary to incumbent Jaime Williams. According to his campaign website, he is an Obama Scholar who has also built a small business, and he is running on lowering costs, protecting homeowners, preventing gun violence, and addressing flooding.

background.text: According to his campaign website, Jalloh is the son of a union nurse and a taxi driver who immigrated to New York, and he was born and raised in Brooklyn.
His campaign describes him as an Obama Scholar, community organizer, and nonprofit CEO.

According to his campaign, he helped stop a pesticide facility from being built near homes and schools, helped secure $1.6 million in funding to prevent gun violence, and supported workers in winning a union.
His campaign says he built a small business, giving him experience meeting payroll and dealing with government red tape.

In 2026 he ran in the Democratic primary for Assembly District 59 and lost to Jaime Williams, 33.8% to 66.0%; he advanced from the Working Families Party primary, which was canceled, and is on the November ballot on that line.

priorities.text: "Lower the Cost of Living: Fund universal childcare, healthcare and expand access to fresh and affordable food."
"Protect Homeowners: Stop deed theft, expand foreclosure prevention programs, support first-time homebuyer grants."
"Economic investment & Small Businesses: Secure funding to revitalize our commercial corridors and push legislation that bolsters our small businesses."
"Invest in Education & Youth: Modernize school facilities, expand after-school and summer programs, and connect students to career and college pathways."
"Fix Flooding & Infrastructure: Upgrade drainage systems, expand green infrastructure, and create emergency relief for flood-impacted families. Fund NYCHA repairs."

researchNotes: Jaime Williams has not completed a Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey in any cycle and has no current campaign website; her recent nyassembly.gov press releases predate the 2025-2026 session, so no current-cycle 'priorities in their own words' statements could be found and researchDepth is marked 'basic' with her record documented from official committee, bill-sponsorship, and floor-vote sources instead. Biographical detail for Jibreel Jalloh comes almost entirely from his own campaign website; no education, employer names, or independent news profile were found, and no prior public office is on record.
